comment: Dr. Salisbury is a great choice if you're looking to fulfill a general education credit! He is very passionate about his work and does everything possible to involve everyone. Homework's are about 10-25 question, projects are given well in advance and exams are fairly simple. My only complaint would be that lectures are relatively disorganized.

The class was mostly chill; discussions based on reading assignments which were usually quite reasonable in length & difficulty. The subjects were all quite essential to learning about human interactions with climate, although David definitely went abstract at times and, towards the end, could seem unwieldy in direction with the course. Overall gr8

A bit disorganized but generally an easy class. It is often boring but he tries to make jokes if he likes your class. If you show any interest or effort, he will give you a good grade. Bear in mind that I was in the Endeavor Course with Dr. Salisbury meaning he was also my advisor.
Easy class, but very disorganized. I wish there was more structure because Dr. Salisbury is so knowledgeable and I feel like I had a lot to learn from him.

Stopped grading homework before midterms, class was just a bunch of talking and no new information, final exam did not reflect what the class content was like. super disorganized and a waste of time, made me hate environmental sustainability. final project was a class project of 18 people,,,

He's humorous, caring, and great at finding the best & weak parts in presentations & work/tests. This class was SO interactive with the city of Richmond and an amazing experience for a first year who is trying to figure out their way through this university. Heavy on applied learning and taking notes on readings before every class. Highly recommend

Easily the nicest and most helpful professor Ive had so far at Richmond. Dr. Salisbury really encourages in class participation but also his students getting involved in other projects/opportunities outside of class. GS 290 had one-medium-sized essay, a midterm, and a final exam, but everything else was standard. Absolutely recommend for GS 290.

I've enjoyed every class I've taken with Dr. Salisbury, GEOG 345 is no different. Lots of long readings but they're always relevant and give you a really robust understanding of the topic. He has high expectations but is accessible outside of class and listens to student feedback. Classes are never boring and he says some pretty funny stuff too.

Great professor! You can tell he really is passionate about the topic. Lots of really interesting projects and readings--you certainly won't get bored with this class! There's quite a bit of group work, but I really enjoyed it. Highly recommend!

I really really enjoyed Professor Salisbury's class. If you are interested in geography or international studies - he is an excellent teacher. Values student feedback and participation. Class style is very discussion based and student lead. I found this very effective. He is creative and strives to keep classes interesting. 100% would take again!!!

To be honest, Dr. Salisbury is the best professor I have had. He is the only teacher I know who takes time out to actually talk about writing, life lessons, and things that actually matter. He recognizes the role of a liberal arts education in developing the student into a well-rounded person. But he is not for everyone.
Incredibly helpful and knowledgeable professor. I spent countless hours in his office getting help for papers and projects. Great resource to conduct useful research.

His teaching style is pretty much nonexistent. He relies too much on student presentations and participation instead of lecturing and he occupies the class with busy work the whole year. I think he just wasn't interested in the class material, but I still wouldn't take him again.

Some of the material is really interesting because it relates to real world events but at other times, the class gets kind of boring because he lectures with a PowerPoint. We did some fun activities but there was a large amount of busy work. He grades tough. He doesn't give As easily so don't take this class for an easy grade.

Dr. Salisbury is an interesting and fun guy. He is a tough grader and expects students to work hard. One thing I don't like about his teaching style is that he is too fond of student participation and doesn't ever lecture. He is always asking what students think about readings or current events. And thats fine, but it gets old after a while.

I forgot the no. of the course. It's like Human Geography or something. Dr. Salisbury is so awesome although his course is hard. He expects a lot from his students, like speaking up in classes and doing presentations really well. But he knows a lot and is passionate in teaching. Would definitely recommend him! He's one of the best I've had in UR!
He jumps around too much and is hard to follow.  I wanted to major in Geography, but since Dr. Mike left I will probably stick to Sociology.
Great guy, If you get the chance.. take one of his courses. Also, very interesting, he has travelled all over the world.
